title: 〜はおろか
simpleExplanation: 〜はおろか takes something big (X) and says "X is out of the question; even the much smaller Y is not possible": 漢字はおろか、ひらがなも読めない (cannot read even hiragana, let alone kanji). The second half has も・さえ・すら plus a negative or a negative-feeling predicate. The tone is emotional: surprise, complaint or pity.
whenUsed: Both speech and writing, moderately formal. Used when the speaker wants to dramatise how bad or how limited a situation is. Not used for neutral facts; there is always a sense of "it's that bad".
formation: N + はおろか、N + も / さえ / すら + negative
N + はおろか、N + も + negative-feeling predicate (ない・できない・時間がない)
The first noun is the harder or bigger item

diagram.title: Order of difficulty in はおろか

items.label: 漢字 (hard)
items.description: はおろか: obviously impossible, not even worth discussing

items.label: ひらがな (easy)
items.description: も読めない: even this easy thing is impossible

examples.ja: 漢字はおろか、ひらがなも読めない。
examples.reading: かんじはおろか、ひらがなもよめない。
examples.en: He cannot read even hiragana, let alone kanji.
examples.note: Hard item (漢字) first, easy item (ひらがな) second, negative at the end.

examples.ja: 彼は海外はおろか、隣の県にさえ行ったことがない。
examples.reading: かれはかいがいはおろか、となりのけんにさえいったことがない。
examples.en: He has never even been to the next prefecture, let alone abroad.
examples.note: Big item (going abroad) → small item (the next prefecture) + さえ + negative.

examples.ja: 忙しくて、旅行はおろか、休日に外出する時間もない。
examples.reading: いそがしくて、りょこうはおろか、きゅうじつにがいしゅつするじかんもない。
examples.en: I am so busy that I have no time to go out on holidays, let alone travel.
examples.note: The negative can be 時間もない: no time even for going out.

examples.ja: 熱が高くて、食事はおろか、水を飲むことさえできなかった。
examples.reading: ねつがたかくて、しょくじはおろか、みずをのむことさえできなかった。
examples.en: With such a high fever, I could not even drink water, let alone eat.
examples.note: 食事 (bigger) → 水 (smaller), with さえ.

examples.ja: 彼は貯金はおろか、来月の家賃すら払えない状態だ。
examples.reading: かれはちょきんはおろか、らいげつのやちんすらはらえないじょうたいだ。
examples.en: He is in a state where he cannot even pay next month's rent, let alone save money.
examples.note: すら is the most formal of the three particles.

similarGrammar.difference: "Far from X, actually Y": corrects an expectation and can be positive or negative. はおろか always builds down to a negative.
"Not limited to X but also Y": scope widens in a positive direction, the opposite of はおろか.
"X of course, and Y too": both are affirmed. はおろか denies both.

commonMistakes.wrong: ひらがなはおろか、漢字も読めない。
commonMistakes.right: 漢字はおろか、ひらがなも読めない。
commonMistakes.why: The first item must be the harder one; otherwise the logic collapses.

commonMistakes.wrong: 漢字はおろか、ひらがなが読める。
commonMistakes.right: 漢字はおろか、ひらがなも読めない。
commonMistakes.why: The second half needs も/さえ and a negative; an affirmative ending is impossible.

commonMistakes.wrong: 彼は英語はおろか、フランス語も話せる。
commonMistakes.right: 彼は英語はもちろん、フランス語も話せる。
commonMistakes.why: For "X of course, and Y too" in a positive sense, use はもちろん.

usageNotes: Think of it as "never mind X, not even Y": the listener is meant to be surprised at how far the negative goes.
The particle after the second noun ranges from も (neutral) to さえ・すら (stronger, more formal).
The predicate can be a negative adjective phrase such as 余裕がない or 時間がない.
jlptTips: Check the two items: if the first is bigger or harder and the ending is negative with も / さえ, はおろか is the answer.
Distractors: どころか, はもちろん, にとどまらず. Only はおろか requires the downward order plus negative.
In 並べ替え, place N + はおろか first, then N + さえ / も, then the negative verb.
